title: Chess for Three
format: A performed exchange (three real posts, in order, each by its author's puppet), then a demonstration: the house sits down at the studio's sketch of the board. The experiment's wordless stretch carries the turn.
retell: A member built chess for three on a Möbius strip; another member would like it and repost it but not love it without a link; then Larry picked his side of the board in gold, the gold ran all the way round both faces, and he resigned before the first move.

rendered.how: Rendered in a scratch folder with the studio's renderer and its Whisper check, with cast.js applied. Nothing was written under episodes/ but this draft.
rendered.whisper: 94 of 110 caption words (85%). Every line's heard text was read.

experiment.stretch: From the end of the line `gold` to the cue `stretch-end`: 11.87 s in the scratch render (39.28 s to 51.15 s). It holds no `say`, `sing` or `shout` line and no audience sound. In it: one music block, `claim`, of two beat tracks (Pete's beat, Al's hummed bass: both kind `beat`), four ticks, two whooshes and a ding.
experiment.whatTheThingDoes: The house sits down at the board and Larry claims a side: his gold flag sets off along the strip, comes back to his own seat underneath and upside down, keeps going, and arrives where it began with every square gold on both faces and the other two players' flags standing on it. The board has one side, and the board is what shows it.
experiment.before: No line before it says what the board will do. Eppy counts the players and the strip, Sibyl says 'Pick a side.', Larry says 'I'll take this side. In gold.'
experiment.after: No line after it says what it did. Sibyl: 'Larry. Your move.' Larry: 'I like. I repost.' 'I resign.' The laugh comes at `stretch-end`, not before.
experiment.onScreenDuringIt: The studio's sketch, labelled STUDIO SKETCH; the credit 'ringmate · mobius.mokkenstorm.dev · by @mokkenstorm.dev'; three name flags (LARRY, SIBYL, EPPY); the travelling flag LARRY'S SIDE. Nothing else to read. No caption, no post card, no lamps.
experiment.forACutOrTrim: Do not shorten the music block or move the laugh before `stretch-end`: the measure needs 10.0 s and the block alone gives 10.25.

howItUsesTheIdeas.writer-2-162: Kept: its turn, the condition ('I like! I repost! But I'm not gonna love unless there's a link'), and the three lamps. Cut, on the project manager's note: the clock, the time jump, the link arriving, the third lamp lighting and the reply to the link. The exchange stops on the condition, so the punch is the condition and not that the thing got built. That also removes the swear. The condition comes back once, as Larry's button.
howItUsesTheIdeas.writer-1-63: Kept: three house players and Larry wanting his side. Changed for the experiment: nobody says there is only one side. Sibyl's line is 'Pick a side.' and the board does the rest without words. Changed for the media notes: no pawn is pushed; what travels is Larry's flag.

engineNotes: 'chess' is a weak word in every voice. It is in no house line and on no punch.
Short lines straight after a laugh were misheard; each laugh now has hold 0.8 before the next line. Keep that room.

The two guest voices sit in the house range's two open spots (median f0 176 Hz and 239 Hz; nearest house voice 1.52 and 2.10). Other drafts' guests may want the same spots: measure them together at assembly.
builder: THE BOARD IS A SKETCH. Nobody here has seen the real board, its rules or a game in play. Draw only: a single file of squares bent into a loop with one half twist, and a circle of chess pieces standing on it (the picture's alt text). Label it STUDIO SKETCH for as long as it is up. Keep the credit 'ringmate · mobius.mokkenstorm.dev · by @mokkenstorm.dev' up with it.

THE PIECES NEVER MOVE. No arrows, no captures, no check, no turn order, nothing labelled RULES. Use plain piece shapes and do not suggest which pieces the real game has. The flag is a flag, not a pawn. Nothing is drawn for 'ghosts and ninjas': nobody knows what they are.

Make the two faces of the strip tell apart at a glance (say, bright squares on top, dimmer or dashed underneath), and put the twist in one visible place, on the far side between Eppy's seat and Larry's. Then one lap reads as: past Sibyl's flag, past Eppy's, through the twist, back under Larry. The flag stands along the surface, so it arrives hanging upside down.

THE STRETCH (cue `claim` to cue `stretch-end`) must keep changing. Beats of `claim` at 96 bpm: 0 the flag sets off; 2.67 and 5.33 it passes Sibyl's and Eppy's flags (ticks); 6.67 the twist (whoosh); 8 it is under Larry's seat, upside down, and does not stop; 10.67 and 13.33 it passes beneath the two flags (ticks); 14.67 the twist again (whoosh); 16 it is home, the right way up, and everything is gold (ding, the beat stops). Then 1.6 s: the gold loop turns slowly so both faces are seen.

HEADS IN THE STRETCH, no mouths: Larry follows his flag, leans to look under the board at `under`, and at `all-gold` looks left, right, then at us. Sibyl does not move at all. Eppy follows the flag and ends looking at his own, which now stands on gold. No caption bar, no sign lit, no audience bob until `stretch-end`.
THE GUESTS ARE NOT AT THE TABLE. Both guest puppets are off screen from `table` to the end. A guest puppet watching Larry lose would be a reaction its account never published.

CARDS: each real line has its post card up for the whole line, words lighting as spoken, with display name, handle, date and like count from sources.json (17 Nov, 2 likes; 18 Nov, 9 likes; 18 Nov, 5 likes). The two replies say what they replied to without naming anyone: REPLY UNDER THE PICTURE, and REPLY TO A QUESTION.

LAMPS: LIKE, REPOST, LOVE are the member's own three words. Under Minor Mobius, LIKE lights on 'like!', REPOST on 'repost!', and LOVE stays dark. Never light LOVE for Minor Mobius and never add a tick, a padlock caption or a verdict: the show does not say what they felt later. At the button the same three lamps are Larry's, in gold: LIKE on 'like.', REPOST on 'repost.', and on 'resign.' the third flips from LOVE to RESIGN and lights, and his flag tips over.
DISCLAIMER from `maker-in` (the first guest): 'Guests are puppets playing posting personas. Parody.'
The maker's display name is '👩‍💻 tbd : Option<name>', exactly. If the font cannot draw part of it, show what it can and the handle; do not replace the name with another.

LOOKS, a suggestion only: a hue and a tee for what each makes, nothing about the person. The maker: print '1D'. Minor Mobius: print '4D' (their own projects this window are four-dimensional). Heads are not likenesses.

The draft gate reads only the episode's cast, so a guest defined in a draft's own cast.js is not a guest to it and that draft's real lines go unchecked at this stage. This draft was checked by hand as above.

The experiment asks for the thing 'shown in use'; the media notes say nobody has seen it in use and the pieces must not be shown moving. Read here as: the house sits down at the studio's sketch and picks sides, which needs only what a Möbius strip is.
'Three players' is from the maker's idea post. The preview is described by the maker as 'multiplayer'; the draft does not say how many the real page seats.
